| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Ico:Locked | Password icon |
| Ico:League | League icon |
| Ico:GameRunning | Game running icon |
| Ico:Lobby | Lobby icon |
| Ico:RuntimeJoin | Runtime join allowed icon |
| Ico:FairCrew | Fair crew icon |
| Ico:Settlement | Settlement score icon |

C4MN_Add_ForceNoDesc = 512: If this flag is specified the description (set with szInfoCaption and shown as a tooltip) of the menu entry is suppressed completely, whereas in contrast passing 0 as szInfoCaption will show the description of idItem.

CreateScriptPlayer.desc:
Initializes a joining script player. Script players appear as regular players from the scripting point of view. They have a crew, wealth, build knowledge, home base material, hostility, teams, etc. However, script players do not have a game view port and they can not be controlled by human users.
Script players can be used to create AI controlled opponent teams in special scenarios.

params.desc: Player color
params.name: dwClr

params.desc: Team-Id. If 0, a team is automatically chosen according to the rules also applied to normal joining players.
params.name: idTeam

params.desc:
Bit mask composed of the following values:
| Bit | Constant | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | CSPF_FixedAttributes | If set, the player is guaranteed to join with the name and color specified in the parameters. Otherwise those preferences might be ignored in case of conflicts with other players' preferences. |
| 1 | CSPF_NoScenarioInit | If true, the scenario initialization (i.e. placement of home base material, clonks, setting of build knowledge, etc.) is not performed for this player. Also, the global callbacks PreInitializePlayer and InitializePlayer to the scenario script and to goal, rule, and environment objects are not performed. Instead, the callback InitializeScriptPlayer(Player number, Team) is made to the object definition specified in idExtraData. The call is made as DefinitionCall (without `this`() object). Using this parameter you can create script-controlled AI players which do not receive the same standard treatment as user-controlled players. |
| 2 | CSPF_NoEliminationCheck | If set, the player will not be eliminated automatically if its crew is empty. |
| 3 | CSPF_Invisible | If set, the player will not show up in player lists such as in the lobby or hostility menu. |
params.name: dwFlags

params.desc: Id which is passed to the InitializePlayer call. Using this id, it is quite simple to create different types of script players. E.g. a scenario could feature AI players with different types of crew members.
params.name: idExtraData

CreateScriptPlayer.remark:
As do normal players, script player join with a slight delay in network games. This means that following the call to CreateScriptPlayer the player will not be immediately available.
That means, actual initialization of that player should happen in the InitializePlayer callback which can use `GetPlayerType`() to check whether this is a script player.
If the script player really needs to be available even before normal player initialization - e.g. as opponent in a single player mission - you could create the player via the SavePlayerInfos.txt component.

Format.desc:
Composes a string of several values. To do this, the specified string is scanned for '%' placeholders which are then replaced by the parameters.
The general syntax for these placeholders is:
`%[length][.precision]type`Except for type all fields are optional. Type specifies the data type of the parameter to be expected. It is one of the following values:
| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| d | Whole number (int) |
| x | Whole number (int), hexadecimal representation (0123456789abcdef) |
| X | Whole number (int), hexadecimal representation (0123456789ABCDEF) |
| i | id (with ids, length and precision parameters do not apply) |
| s | String |

GetKiller.remark:
Because of the complexity of the Clonk game world it is not always possible to find the actual cause of damage in chain reactions. To track damage, every object stores a controlling player: the number of the player who last controlled, threw, pushed, shot, etc. the object (for details see `GetController`). This field is used to determine the player causing damage:
- Object hits: the controlling player of the thrown object. For items this is set automatically when they are collected. In clonk-to-clonk fights the controlling player of the opponent counts directly as the cause, which is normally the owner.
- Fire: the controller of whoever originally caused the fire, i.e. the calling object of `Incinerate` calls. The cause is passed on through chains of ignition, regardless of owners or controlling players of the burning objects. If, for example, player A sets fire to a clonk of player B, which then ignites a clonk of player C, both fires count as caused by player A.

The damage cause of a clonk is automatically reset to NO_OWNER (no player) when the clonk performs an activity that doesn't have ObjectDisabled=1 set (for example "Walk").
Self-inflicted damage only sets the field to the clonk's own player if it was NO_OWNER before. This prevents a player from taking points away from other players by quickly committing suicide. If a clonk falls out at the bottom, the last player who caused damage counts as the killer; if the clonk was knocked down by a thrown rock, the rock thrower counts.

Determines the value of an object. With idDef specified, the standard value of the original object definition is returned, otherwise the current value of the specified object (pObj) or the calling object if pObj is 0.
An object's value is determined as follows: with pObj specified it is first checked whether the CalcValue function is defined in the object's script and if so, it is evaluated. Otherwise, the definition value is used (see below). The resulting value is then reduced according to the object's completion.
Dead animals or clonks always have value 0.
The definition value is determined as follows: if the function CalcDefValue is defined in the definition script, it is evaluated. Otherwise, the value overload from Scenario.txt is used, if present. Otherwise, the standard value from DefCore is used.

When removing an object, numerous internal references to the object are cleared and any pointer to the object will become invalid. If you have stored a pointer to this object (e.g. in thread local script) you must no longer use this pointer after deletion of the object. SetScoreboardData.desc:
Sets data in the scoreboard. The scoreboard is a global data table which can be used by scenarios to keep track of each player's score or other data. By default, the scoreboard can be displayed with the Tab key but display can also be controlled using `DoScoreboardShow`.
The scoreboard is automatically created when data is set and automatically removed when all data is cleared.
Data is set using a row and column index. If the row or column of a specified index does not yet exist, it is created as soon as data in this row or column is set. It does not matter which numeric indices you use as long as they are unique. So you could also use player numbers, player IDs (see `GetPlayerID`), or team IDs (see `GetPlayerTeam`) as row or column index. In order to prevent different object scripts from accidentally using the same row or column index you can use the `ScoreboardCol` function which will create a unique column index from a given value. In this case you should still take care that all object scripts accessing the scoreboard are using matching row indices. Rows and columnd are not sorted by row or column index. You can use the `SortScoreboard` function for user defined sorting.

params.desc: Value greater than to equal to 0 or SBRD_Caption. Index of the row in which you want to set data. The constant SBRD_Caption indicates the first column which is to be used as column header.
params.name: iRowID

params.name: iColID

params.desc:
Text data to be set. If unspecified or 0, the cell is cleared. If a row is completely empty except for the header (SBRD_Caption), the row is removed. The same applies to columns. Row or column removal is only performed after clearing of a cell.
To display symbols or text in different colors you can use markup.
params.name: sText

params.desc: Extra data for these cells. This data is used to sort the scoreboard using `SortScoreboard`.
params.name: iData

SetScoreboardData.remark: The cell in the top left corner is never displayed. Instead, the value for iRowID == SBRD_Caption and iColID == SBRD_Caption is displayed in the header. If no value is specified here, the scoreboard will not have a header and can not be moved using the mouse.

params.name: iHgt

params.desc: X target position of the SolidMask relative to the top left corner of the object graphic
params.name: iTx

params.desc: Y target position of the SolidMask relative to the top left corner of the object graphic
params.name: iTx

params.desc: Object the solid area of which you want to change. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

SetSolidMask.remark: Solid areas will internally be drawn in the landscape using the "Vehicle" material.

params.desc: Temperature from -100 to 100.
params.name: iTemperature

SetTransferZone.desc: Sets the transfer zone of an object. If the pathfinding trail of another object leads through this transfer zone (a transfer zone is always considered completely passable in pathfinding) ControlTransfer calls will be made to the transfer zone object for the passing clonk. In these calls, the necessary script commands should be given to the clonk so he can pass the object and reach his destination.

params.desc: X position of the top left corner of the new transfer zone, relative to the object center
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y position of the top left corner of the new transfer zone, relative to the object center
params.name: iY

params.desc: Width of the new transfer zone
params.name: iWdt

params.desc: Height of the new transfer zone
params.name: iHgt

params.desc: Object the transfer zone of which you want to change. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

SetTransferZone.remark: Transfer zones have to be set anew when the object has moved. Also, they should be set anew in response to a UpdateTransferZone callback made by the engine.

SetVertex.desc: Sets the offset coordinates of a given object vertex (seeDefCore.txt). Coordinates are relative to the object center.

params.desc: Index of the vertex to be changed.
params.name: iIndex

params.desc: Determines which vertex data is to be changed. 0=VTX_X, 1=VTX_Y, 2=VTX_CNAT, 3=VTX_Friction. Extended since CE.
params.name: iValueToSet

params.desc: Coordinate value to be set.
params.name: iValue

params.desc: Object the vertices of which you want to change. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

params.desc: Special vertex mode. If 1 or 2 the new value will be stored in the last 25 vertices and copied from there during the next shape update. Using this parameter, script changed vertices will be kept during stretch or rotation operations. With value 2, vertices will be updated immediately, not only with the next shape update. Since CE.
params.name: iSetCustomPermanent

SetVertex.remark: Notice: with any vertex updated caused by stretching or rotation of the object (e.g. building or growth) the vertices will be reset to their original defined position unless a special vertex mode is selected using the iSetCustomPermanent parameter.

SetViewCursor.desc: Sets the player's view to pTargetView.

params.desc: Player whose view cursor should be changed.
params.name: iPlr

params.desc: Object to which the view should be set to.
params.name: pTargetView

SetViewOffset.desc: Moves the view of a player permanently by a given offset. Calling the function again will set a new offset. Calling the function with 0,0 parameters will reset to normal, centered view.

params.desc: Player whose view offset you want to change.
params.name: iPlayer

params.desc: X offset value in pixels.
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y offset value in pixels.
params.name: iX

SetVisibility.desc: Changes the visibility of an object. Objects can be made invisible for any group of players by providing a bit mask in dwVisibility.

params.desc:
Bit mask defining the new visibility.
Either `VIS_All`, `VIS_OverlayOnly` or `VIS_None`, or a bit mask of `VIS_Owner`, `VIS_Allies`, `VIS_Enemies`, `VIS_God` and `VIS_Local`.
params.name: dwVisibility

params.desc: Object the visibility of which is to be changed. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

SetWealth.desc: Sets the wealth value of a player.

params.desc: Player number of the player whose wealth should be changed
params.name: iPlr

params.desc: New wealth value.
params.name: iValue

SetWind.desc: Temporarily sets the global wind velocity and direction.

params.desc: Wind velocity from -100 to 100.
params.name: iWind

SetXDir.desc: Sets the horizontal speed of an object.

params.desc: Horizontal speed divided by iPrecision.
params.name: iXDir

params.desc: Target object. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

params.desc: Precision. Default 10 if not specified or 0.
params.name: iPrecision

SetYDir.desc: Sets the vertical speed of an object.

params.desc: Vertical speed divided by iPrecision.
params.name: iYDir

params.desc: Target object. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

params.desc: Precision. Default 10 if not specified or 0.
params.name: iPrecision

ShakeFree.desc: Loosens instable material within a circular area. Loosened material will then begin to fall if there is room underneath. This can be used to collapse earth tunnels or similar.

params.desc: X center position of the circular area to be shaken free. Always global.
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y center position of the circular area to be shaken free. Always global.
params.name: iY

params.desc: Radius of the circular area to be shaken free
params.name: iRadius

ShakeObjects.desc: Shakes all living beings within a given radius. This is comparable to calls to `Fling`() with low random values to all objects in the target area.

params.desc: X center position of the circular area to be shaken. Always global.
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y center position of the circular area to be shaken. Always global.
params.name: iY

params.desc: Radius of the circular area to be shaken
params.name: iRadius

ShiftContents.desc: Resorts the contained objects to the next object with a differing ID will be in front. The most common application for this command is inventory selection.

params.desc: Object the content of which is to be shifted. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

params.desc: If true, objects will be resorted backwards.
params.name: fShiftBack

params.desc: ID of the object type to be in front after the shift. If this parameter is specified, no call to ControlContents will be made. The object will be selected directly and without the selection sound. In this way you can overload the contents switching in ControlContents and add your own sounds or special events.
params.name: idTarget

params.desc: If true, calls to ControlContents and Selection will be made.
params.name: fDoCalls

ShiftContents.remark: This command calls the function "ControlContents" in the container object which can be used to overload the selection process. If the function ControlContents does not exist in the container object or returns 0, the function "Selection" will be called in the newly selected inventory object. If the function Selection does not exist in the contained object or returns 0, the engine will play the "Grab" sound effect for the container object (default behaviour for inventory selection). See also object scripts.

ShowInfo.desc: Displays the description text of an object in a popup window (a menu window).

params.desc: Object for which to display information. If unspecified, the calling object will be used.
params.name: pObject

ShowInfo.remark: The information window's background will be the definition image of the obect.

SimFlight.desc:
Simulates the motion of a falling object with a given starting position and initial speed. If the projected trajectory encounters a material of the specified density, the simulation will stop and the function will return 'true'. Otherwise the function will return 'false'.
If the return value is 'true', the x and y coordinates of the point of interception will be stored in the specified variables for iX and iY, the horizontal and vertical speed at the time of interception in iXDir and iYDir respectively. See references for details.

params.desc: X coordinate of the starting position. Always global.
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y coordinate of the starting position. Always global.
params.name: iY

params.desc: Initial horizontal speed.
params.name: iXDir

params.desc: Initial vertical speed.
params.name: iYDir

params.desc: Mininum density of the material which will stop the projected trajectory. If not specified or 0 this will default to value 50 (solid material).
params.name: iMinDensity

params.desc: Maximum density of the material which will stop the projected trajectory. If not specified or 0 this will default to value 100 (Vehicle).
params.name: iMaxDensity

params.desc: Number of simulated frames for which the projection runs. If not specified or 0 the simultion will run indefinitely until material or the limits of the landscape are encountered.
params.name: iIteration

params.desc: Precision. Default 10 if not specified or 0.
params.name: iPrecision

params.desc: Angle in degrees
params.name: iAngle

params.desc: Radius
params.name: iRadius

params.desc: If specified, the angle will be divided by this value. An angle of 445° and a precision value of 10 will thus result in a more precise angle of 45,5° internally.
params.name: iPrec

Smoke.desc: Creates smoke at the specified position with specified color.

params.desc: X position of the smoke. In a local call this is an offset.
params.name: iX

params.desc: Y position of the smoke. In a local call this is an offset.
params.name: iY

params.desc: Size of the smoke
params.name: iLevel

params.desc: Color of the smoke
params.name: dwClr

SortScoreboard.desc: Sorts scoreboard lines by the extra data of a column. If two entries have the same value in this column, no sorting is done. In this way you can sort these entries by additional columns in subsequent calls to this function.

params.desc: ID of the column by which you want to sort.
params.name: iColID

params.desc: If true, sorting will be done in descendnig order. Otherwise ascending order.
params.name: fReverse

Sound.desc: Plays a sound. The specified sound file has to be available in the group Sound.c4g, in the active scenario file, or in any loaded object definition. The audibility of object local sounds will depend on the position of the object relative to the visible viewports.

params.desc: Name of the sound effect (without .wav ending)
params.name: szSound

params.desc: Specifies wether the sound is played globally, i.e. independently of the object position always with the same loudness.
params.name: fGlobal

params.desc: Object which is to play back the specified sound. Can be 0 in local calls. The object's visible position relative to a player's viewport is responsible for audible volume.
params.name: pObj

params.desc: 0-100: volume for playback of the sound. A volume value of 0 means playback at full volume (default).
params.name: iVolume

params.desc: Player number of the player for which the sound is to be played, increased by 1. In network games, the sound will thus no be audible for the other players. Notice: the player number to be specified has to be increased by 1 since the number 0 is already used for the default (audible for all players)!
params.name: iPlayer

params.desc: Increases or decreases the number of sounds running in a continuous loop. Value +1 will play this sound indefinitely until it is stopped by calling this function again with value -1. Value 0 will play the sound once normally.
params.name: iLoopCount

params.desc: If true, the same sound may be played multiple times at the same time.
params.name: fMultiple

params.desc: Determines how fast the volume decreases depending on the distance.
params.name: iCustomFalloffDistance

SoundLevel.desc: Plays a sound effect in a continuous loop until it is stopped manually. If pObj is not specified, the sound position is global so the sound will be equally audible everywhere in the landscape.

params.desc: Name of the sound effect (without .wav ending)
params.name: szSound

params.desc: 0-100: volume for playback of the sound. A volume value of 0 stops playback.
params.name: iVolume

params.desc: If specified, the sound is played for this object. From 4.9.6.0 CR
params.name: pObj

SoundLevel.remark: As the function will fail if the sound is already playing you should manually stop the sound first.

Split2Components.desc: Splits an object into its components. The new component objects will be created with random rotation and a low speed in random direction at the position at which the object was located. The original object is removed. If the original object was contained, the new component objects will be created in the original container.

params.desc: Object to be split. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

Sqrt.desc: Returns the square root of the first parameter. If the parameter is less than 0, the result is 0.

params.desc: Value of which you want to take the square root
params.name: iValue

params.desc: If specified, only script functions of the given object definition are measured.
params.name: idDefScript

StartScriptProfiler.remark: The script profiler can be used to measure how much processing time the scripting engine is using for executing certain script functions. This can be useful to find out which parts of a script are mainly slowing down execution in larger scenarios. The profiler measures the execution time between the commands StartScriptProfiler and StopScriptProfiler.

StopScriptProfiler.desc: Stops the script profiler and writes the result to the log.
StopScriptProfiler.remark: The script profiler can be used to measure how much processing time the scripting engine is using for executing certain script functions. This can be useful to find out which parts of a script are mainly slowing down execution in larger scenarios. The profiler measures the execution time between the commands StartScriptProfiler and StopScriptProfiler.

Stuck.desc: Returns whether an object is stuck, meaning that one of its vertices is enclosed in solid matter.

params.desc: Object of which you want to know if it's stuck. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObject

TestMessageBoard.desc: Tests if a message board input query (created by `CallMessageBoard`) exists. Also returns true if `CallMessageBoard` has been called and the query has been queued, but the input has not been shown yet.

params.desc: Player for who the message board should be tested.
params.name: iPlr

params.desc: Whether to test really.
params.name: fTestIfInUse

TrainPhysical.desc: Increases the physical property of an object by the specified value. This function will train permanent physicals as well as temporary physicals. This function can be used e.g. to enhance magic capabilities after casting spells.

params.desc: Name of property to be changed
params.name: szPhysical

params.desc: 0-100000: added training value
params.name: iTrainBy

params.desc: Maximum training value. In no case, the physical property of the clonk will be modified, even if its value is lower than the value specified here.
params.name: iMaxTrain

params.desc: Object the physicals of which you want to change. Can be 0 in local calls.
params.name: pObj

UnselectCrew.desc: Deselects the complete crew of a player. After this command you should reselect a new clonk using `SelectCrew`.

params.desc: Player whose crew you want to deselect.
params.name: iPlr

Value.desc: Returns a property of a definition.

params.desc: ID of the definition of which you want to request a property.
params.name: idDef

Value.remark: Calling Value() does not invoke a call to CalcDefValue() but directly returns the DefCore value of the definition (notice this might have been overloaded in Scenario.txt). You should use `GetValue` instead with proper parameters.

VarN.desc: Returns a reference to a function local variable. This reference can be used for reading or writing.

params.desc: Name of the variable to which a reference is to be returned
params.name: szName

WildcardMatch.desc: Returns whether to strings are equal. The comparison is case sensitive and wildcards are supported.

params.desc: String to compare.
params.name: szStr

params.desc: String to compare.
params.name: szWildcard

WildcardMatch.remark: A * can represent any number of unknown characters (including none). A ? represents exactly one unknown character.

params.desc: Script to be executed
params.name: strScript

goto.desc: Sets the script counter for scenario scripts to the specified value. The script counter is responsible for calling the ScriptXXX functions in a scenario script. This does not apply to object scripts - those should be using TimerCall or ActMaps with StartCall/PhaseCall/EndCall.

params.desc: New value for the script counter. The next scenario script function called will be ScriptXXX.
params.name: iCounter

goto.remark: In older script versions goto() would also cause an immediate `return`(). This behaviour has changed with the #strict standard. Now you have to write your `return`() separately.

this.desc: Returns a pointer to the object in the scope of which the script is currently being executed.
this.remark: The parameter brackets can be omitted.
